title: Dish record (dish_…)
description: A fully formed, selectable unit of infrastructure (glossary: Dish). Everything that affects behaviour, topology or cost is fixed in the record; its only inputs are names, placements and wires (R3). `provides` is a value of exactly one kind (R2, decision 28); `recipe` names exactly one recipe (R4, decision 33). What an agent reads to decide whether the dish satisfies a need is `provides`, the ports and the attestations about this address — never the recipe (decision 22). Unsigned; a changed anything is a new dish.

of_kind.description: The one kind this dish provides a value of.

provides.description: A value-expression `record` conforming to the kind's attributes type. Publication fails if a field is missing, unknown or wrongly typed (R2).

names.description: Name inputs: literal resource names the instance supplies (decision 29). A composite's components' names are derived from these by the recipe's fixed rules and ALSO written out in the instance, which the provisioning command checks.

count.description: For `regions`: how many the instance must supply, matching `provides`.

placements.description: Placement inputs the instance supplies: project, region(s), zone, name-service zone.

wires.description: Typed input ports. A wire binds another serving's output port of the SAME type (structural equality of the canonical type expressions) to one of these; a credential input has the secret-reference type (decision 31).

outputs.description: Typed output ports. Values are produced at kitchen time and land in the receipt; a secret-bearing output is a secret reference, never a value.

recipe.description: Exactly one recipe. A changed recipe is a new dish (decision 33).

supersedes.description: Lineage only; the mechanism never follows it (principle 1). A succession statement carries the reason.
